title: Hotel or Apartment in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **The three options are priced in three different shapes.** A hotel charges per room and a room sleeps two, an apartment charges per flat whatever the party size but adds a one-off cleaning fee, and hostel beds charge per person per night. The cheapest one therefore changes with your group size and your length of stay.

**Berlin taxes all of them at 7.5 %** of the net accommodation price, hotels, hostels, guesthouses and holiday flats alike. Breakfast and parking sit outside that base. Business travel lost its exemption on 1 April 2024, and the old ten-bed threshold for small operators disappeared on 1 January 2026.

**Check the registration number before you pay for a flat.** Berlin requires every whole-flat holiday listing to show a district-issued registration number, publicly visible, and the Senate says it is 17 characters long. No number, no booking.

**EU Regulation 2024/1028 has applied since 20 May 2026.** Platforms must now verify those numbers and report host data to a national digital entry point, so an unregistered Berlin listing is far more likely to vanish between booking and arrival. The host risks the fine; you risk the cancellation.
**Odd numbers of travellers punish hotels.** Three people means two rooms and you pay for the empty half of one. That single effect is often what tips a trip towards a flat or towards beds.
**The cleaning fee is a short-stay problem, not a long-stay one.** On two nights it can be a fifth of the bill. Spread over eight nights nobody notices it, which is why apartments win longer trips.
**A reception desk is worth money on exactly one night: the night you arrive.** If you land late at BER, that is the difference between a key and a wait in a dark Hinterhof.
